transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thank you, doctor. It's a lovely office you have here. The plants are just beautiful. I used to have a spider plant just like that one in the corner, but my cat—oh, he passed away a few years ago, bless his heart—he used to chew on the leaves constantly. 

But anyway, my daughter thought I should come in because... well, for the past year or so, I feel like I’m just always puttering around. Fixing things, arranging the cupboards, volunteering for just one more thing at the church. Even at 87, I have a hard time just sitting down and being still! 

Like last Tuesday, I was supposed to be resting and watching my programs, but I noticed the hinges on the pantry door were squeaking, and before I knew it, I had the whole toolbox out. That toolbox belonged to my late husband, Arthur. He bought it at a Sears back in 1972... or was it '73? We had just moved to the house on Elm Street, the one with the big oak tree in the front yard. The roots on that tree caused us so much trouble with the plumbing, we had to have a man come out three times in one winter just to clear the pipes... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, yes. I just can't seem to stop moving and doing things, and my family thinks it's a bit much.
Have you noticed a change in how much sleep you need to feel fully energized?

Sleep? Goodness, no, I don't think so. I've always needed about the same amount, and I still get my seven hours. Though, I do wake up quite early. Usually right around 5:30. That's when the birds start at the feeder outside my bedroom window. 

I put out suet for the woodpeckers, you know. Oh, they just love it! But you have to be careful which brand you buy, because the cheap ones melt in the summer heat and make a terrible, sticky mess on the patio. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she bought the cheap kind once and her golden retriever ate it right off the bricks. Oh, that poor dog had an upset stomach for two days. She had to feed him boiled chicken and rice... 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh! My sleep. Yes. No, no changes there. I sleep just fine, I just get up and get going!

{"intent": "Assess whether the patient's constant activity and restlessness are driven by excessive worry or anxiety to evaluate for generalized anxiety disorder", "question": "Do you find

Do I find myself worrying? Oh, heavens no. I'm not much of a worrier at all. I leave all the worrying to my sister, Martha. Now, she could worry the stripes off a zebra! She used to call me every time there was a thunderstorm warning, convinced the roof was going to blow right off the house. 

We grew up in Kansas, you see, so tornadoes were a real thing back then. I remember one time in 1948... or maybe it was '49? Yes, '49, because I had just gotten this beautiful yellow gingham dress for my birthday. Anyway, the sirens went off and we had to go hide down in the root cellar. My mother kept all her jars of pickled beets down there. I can't even look at a pickled beet to this day without smelling that damp earth. 

But Martha, she still watches the Weather Channel all day long like it's a soap opera. That man on there, the one with the nice teeth... Jim something? He's always standing out in the rain. I just don't know why they make those poor reporters stand in the hurricane wind. They could just look out a window and tell us it's raining! 

But, oh... I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Was it about Martha? Oh, right, worrying. No, no, I don't feel anxious or anything like that. I just have a lot of pep and I like to get things done!
Do you need any help from your daughter or others with managing everyday tasks, like paying bills, taking medications, or keeping track of appointments?

Help from my daughter? Oh, goodness no. I manage all my own affairs, thank you very much. I pay my bills on time, take my vitamins... well, I do use one of those little plastic boxes with the days of the week on it. My daughter bought it for me at the pharmacy. 

It's a nice pharmacy, the one over on Main Street. The pharmacist there, David, he's such a polite young man. He always asks about my garden. He told me his tomatoes were getting blossom end rot last year, and I told him, "David, you need to put some crushed eggshells in the soil!" That's what my grandmother always did. She had a garden the size of a football field back in Ohio. She used to grow these massive beefsteak tomatoes, big as your head! We would slice them thick, put a little mayonnaise and black pepper on white bread... oh, there is nothing like a fresh tomato sandwich in August. 

The tomatoes you buy at the grocery store nowadays, they taste like cardboard, don't they? They pick them when they're green and hard as rocks, and then they spray them with some sort of gas to make them turn red. It's just not natural. I read an article in the Reader's Digest about it once while I was waiting at the dentist's office. Dr. Peterson, he's my dentist. He has the most fascinating collection of antique toothbrushes in his waiting room...

Oh, dear, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I just start talking and the thoughts just tumble right out! What was the question? Oh, needing help. No, no, I do everything myself. I'm sharp as a tack, I just can't sit still!
Aside from having lots of energy, have you been feeling unusually high, elated, or on top of the world?

Unusually high? Like... like I'm on top of the world? Oh, no, nothing like that. I'm just happy, you know? I've always been a cheerful person. My husband, God rest his soul, used to say I was the sunshine in his day. He was a very quiet man, my Arthur. He worked at the bank for forty-two years, sitting at the same desk. 

He had this terrible habit of chewing on the ends of his pens. I used to buy him those nice gold-plated Cross pens for Christmas, but he'd just ruin them! He said it helped him think. I don't know how anyone could think with a mouthful of ink. One time, one of those cheap plastic ones burst in his pocket and ruined a perfectly good white dress shirt. I tried everything to get the stain out—lemon juice, baking soda, even hairspray! Hairspray is wonderful for ink stains, did you know that? The aerosol kind, not the pump spray. Aqua Net is the best. I used to go through a can a week back in the sixties when I wore my hair in a beehive. Oh, the time it took to tease all that hair! And sleeping on it... you had to wrap your head in toilet paper so it wouldn't get squished...

Wait, what were we talking about? Arthur's shirts? No, no... oh! Feeling high or elated. No, dear, I don't feel like that. I'm just my regular self, just with a lot of pep!
Have you noticed any problems with your memory recently, such as forgetting recent conversations or events?

Memory problems? Oh, goodness, no. My memory is sharp as a tack! I remember things just fine. Why, just yesterday I was telling my neighbor, Mrs. Higgins—she lives in that lovely blue house on the corner with the wrap-around porch—I was telling her about the time we went to the World's Fair in New York. 

That was 1964, you know. They had this enormous globe, the Unisphere. It was just spectacular. We took the train all the way from Chicago. I wore a smart little navy suit with white piping and a pillbox hat. Jackie Kennedy made those hats so popular, didn't she? I had one in almost every color to match my shoes. Shoes used to be made so much better back then. Real leather, not this synthetic stuff that makes your feet sweat. I bought a pair of loafers last month at the mall, and they gave me the most terrible blister on my heel. I had to use three Band-Aids just to walk to the mailbox! 

The mailman, Gary, he's such a sweet boy. He always makes sure to put my magazines inside the screen door so they don't get wet if it rains. He has a golden retriever that just had puppies. Seven little blond furballs! I told him I'd love to take one, but I just don't have the time to train a puppy. They chew on everything, you know. My cousin's dog ate the leg right off her antique dining table...

Oh, dear me, I'm doing it again. My mind just goes a mile a minute! What did you ask me? Memory? Yes, right. No, I don't forget things. I remember all my conversations and everything else. I just have so many things to say!
